holidays.name: National Dance Like a Chicken Day
holidays.description: Flap your wings, snap your beak, and wiggle your tail feathers. This is a day for doing the Chicken Dance with zero dignity and maximum joy. Weddings, birthday parties and office break rooms are all fair game.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that celebrates the Chicken Dance, a tune that began as a Swiss accordion melody written by Werner Thomas in the late 1950s. The song grew into a worldwide party staple, and the day honors its silly legacy.
holidays.funFact: The Chicken Dance melody started life as a Swiss accordion tune. It later spread across the world and became a fixture at Oktoberfests, weddings and kids' parties.

holidays.name: National Buttermilk Biscuit Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the fluffy, flaky, butter-ready biscuit. Split one warm from the oven and add butter, honey, jam or gravy. Breakfast, lunch and dinner all qualify.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that celebrates a classic American comfort food. Biscuits grew out of hardtack, a cheap, long-lasting bread made from flour and water. Baking powder and soda later made them light and fluffy.
holidays.funFact: The word biscuit comes from an old French phrase meaning twice-baked. Today's soft, fluffy Southern biscuit is a very different bread from the dry, hard ancestor it came from.

holidays.name: National Underground America Day
holidays.description: This day is for appreciating everything hidden beneath our feet, including caves, subways, tunnels, bunkers and the cozy basements of the nation. It's a good excuse to explore the world below the surface.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It was later popularized online and in pop culture, and it is listed on May 14 in national day calendars.
holidays.funFact: The day got a burst of attention when it was tied to viral marketing for the 2019 horror film Us, which is set around a hidden underground world.
